## Before you start {.study}

- **What you need:** PowerPoint (the desktop app, PowerPoint on the web at
  `office.com`, or the free phone app) and a free AI chat tool (for example
  Microsoft Copilot with your university account, ChatGPT or Gemini).
  An AI image tool is optional: stock images also work.
- **Time:** about 60 minutes. Work alone, at your own speed.
- **How it works:** do Steps 1–3 on this page. Each step has a short text, a
  simulator and a self-check. Then do the **Tasks to submit**.
- **What you submit:** one PowerPoint file and one Word file with your
  prompts and short answers, before lecture 21.
- **You need lectures 17–19:** layouts, themes, few words, speaker notes,
  outlines and image prompts.
- **Never type personal data into an AI tool**: no names, phone numbers or
  marks of real people.

## Key terms {.study}

{{< glossary presentation-outline outline-view image-prompt ai-image stock-image speaker-notes check-ai-output hallucination >}}

## Step 1 · An outline with AI {.study}

- Choose a topic you know, for example *a study tip that works for me*, *a
  free app that helps students*, or *how our college can save paper*.
- Prompt with five parts: **topic, audience** (your classmates), **length**
  (5 slides, 3 minutes), **form** (title + 3 points), **limit** (8 words per
  point). Add: "Do not invent numbers or sources."
- Read the answer. Mark every number and source: you will check them in
  Step 3.

![A clear prompt gives a short outline.](images/outline-prompt.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/outline-lab.html" poster="sims/outline-lab.png" title="Outline Lab: from an AI outline to slides" height="1040" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The outline"}
Use Outline Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Ctrl+S|Insert › Video"}
How many slides has the fixed outline?
:   5

Which key makes a line a point?
:   Tab

Where do the outline lines go in PowerPoint?
:   View › Outline

What happens to the made-up source?
:   it is deleted
:::
:::

## Step 2 · Slides and one picture {.study}

- Paste the outline into **View › Outline**, fix the levels with **Tab** and
  **Shift+Tab**, and choose one **theme**.
- Title Slide for slide 1, Title and Content for the others (lecture 17).
- One picture for one slide: an **image prompt** with subject, style,
  setting, colours, shape and "no text", or a **stock image**
  (Insert › Pictures › Stock Images).
- Check the picture closely, write **alt text**, and add the note
  "Picture: AI-generated" if an AI made it.

![Errors to look for in an AI picture.](images/ai-pictures.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/image-prompt-lab.html" poster="sims/image-prompt-lab.png" title="Image Prompt Lab: a picture for a slide" height="900" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The picture"}
Use Image Prompt Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a famous singer|tall 9:16"}
the shape for a slide picture
:   wide 16:9

what to ask about text
:   no text in the picture

the note for an AI picture
:   Picture: AI-generated

if the AI picture has errors
:   use a stock image
:::
:::

## Step 3 · Check, add notes, rehearse {.study}

- **Facts and sources:** compare every number with a source you trust;
  delete any source you cannot open.
- **Your words:** write the **speaker notes** of each slide yourself, two
  or three sentences (lecture 18).
- **Few words** on the slides: 3–5 points of at most 8 words.
- On the last slide: a short note on what the AI did.
- Rehearse once with Presenter View and the timer: about three minutes.

![Five checks before the talk.](images/check-deck.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/ai-deck-check.html" poster="sims/ai-deck-check.png" title="AI Deck Check: ready for Monday?" kind="game" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Checks"}
Use AI Deck Check. Choose the best action.

::: {.match extra="keep it|make the font smaller"}
a number that your notes do not show
:   check it and correct it

a source that you cannot find
:   delete it

staff names in a prompt
:   take them out

a slide with five long sentences
:   3–5 short points
:::
:::

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

Do the tasks alone. Your teacher marks them (6 marks). Use only your own
topic and no personal data of other people.

### Task 1 · The outline (2 marks)

1. Write your outline prompt with the five parts and get an outline from an
   AI tool.
2. In a Word file `my-prompts.docx`, paste your prompt and the AI answer,
   and mark (highlight) every number and source you had to check.

### Task 2 · Five slides (2 marks)

1. Make `my-ai-talk.pptx` from the outline with Outline view: five slides,
   one theme, the right layouts, at most five short points per slide.
2. Add one picture (AI-generated and checked, or a stock image) with alt
   text, and speaker notes in your own words on every slide.
3. On the last slide, add a short note on what the AI did.

### Task 3 · Your check (2 marks)

Answer in `my-prompts.docx`:

a) Which number or source from the AI did you check? Was it right? What
did you change?

{{< answer-space lines=3 >}}

b) Name two changes you made to the AI outline or picture, and say why.

{{< answer-space lines=3 >}}

## How to submit

Upload `my-ai-talk.pptx` and `my-prompts.docx` to the university
e-learning platform, **before lecture 21**.
